Tufte's colour palettes

Source: R/scales.R
tufte_pal.Rd

Four palettes, each answering a different question about colour.

Usage

tufte_pal(palette = c("grey", "accent", "muted", "divergent"))

tufte_colours(palette = c("grey", "accent", "muted", "divergent"))

tufte_colors(palette = c("grey", "accent", "muted", "divergent"))

Arguments

palette

One of "grey", "accent", "muted", "divergent".

Value

For tufte_pal(), a function of n returning n colours. For tufte_colours(), a character vector of hex colours.

Details

"grey"

Tufte's default. Grey encodes an ordered variable without introducing a second, unwanted, categorical signal.

"accent"

Greys plus one signal red. Use when exactly one series matters and the rest are context. This is the palette that does the most work in Envisioning Information: layering by value, not by hue.

"muted"

Desaturated earth tones, after the maps and timetables Tufte reproduces. Colours this weak sit behind text and annotation without fighting them.

"divergent"

A muted blue-to-red ramp for signed quantities, with a neutral rather than a white midpoint.

Examples

tufte_pal("muted")(4)
#> [1] "#7c6a55" "#8a9a5b" "#9c6b6b" "#5b7c8a"
tufte_colours("accent")
#> [1] "#8c8c8c" "#b3b3b3" "#c8102e" "#d9d9d9" "#595959"
